summary: This note covers the 2017 FIFA Confederations Cup, whose host Russia was announced on 2 December 2010 after being awarded the 2018 FIFA World Cup. The matches were played in four stadiums across Saint Petersburg, Moscow, Kazan and Sochi. It was Russia's first time hosting the tournament and the third time the Confederations Cup was held in Europe. Russia qualified automatically as hosts, joined by six confederation champions and 2014 World Cup winners Germany.
one_line: Overview of the 2017 FIFA Confederations Cup, hosted by Russia across four cities, with its qualification structure.
key_facts: Russia was announced as the host of the 2017 FIFA Confederations Cup on 2 December 2010.
Russia was announced as host after the country was awarded the hosting rights of the 2018 FIFA World Cup.
The matches were played in four different stadiums across four cities.
The four host cities were Saint Petersburg, Moscow, Kazan, and Sochi.
It was the first time Russia has hosted the Confederations Cup tournament.
It was the third time the Confederations Cup has been held in the European continent.
As hosts, Russia qualified automatically for the tournament.
Russia was joined by the six winners of the FIFA confederation championships.
Germany was included as the 2014 FIFA World Cup champions.
Germany joined Russia and the six confederation champions in the tournament field.
